chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Recording Olga Guillot at Nola Studios
summary: The band backed Olga Guillot on twelve numbers, arranged by Rene Hernandez, for a few bottles of liquor; Chano may have played conga.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Ah - Ha. Machito, this recordings took place in 1946. There's a photograph where - in which the entire Machito orchestra is at the Nola Penthouse Studios. Olga Guillot is there, Tito Rodriguez, Arsenio Rodriguez and his brother Quique are there and Chano Pozo is there. Do you remember that day when that picture was photographed?

Sure, that was a great moment because there was so many people that we know each other for years, so, like a happy reunion because I knew Olga when she was very young. The time that I was in Havana, I think it was nineteen - early forties, and she was starting because she was singing with a group and she was part of the group like Las Aidas or other groups that they was organized in Havana and in those days seems like there was a revolution about quartets and quintets. The girls and Marcelino Guerra was - belong to one of them, when Olga Guillot was singing.
But you knew of her already when she came to the United States, right?
Okay, she wasn't started yet, Miguelito got her that recording date and I heard that the first tune - she did twelve numbers with your band - was "Sangre Son Colora"
Now, I understand that the Machito orchestra didn't get paid for that session.

Well, like always, we were so enthusiastic to back up a good singer. It wasn't nothing of patriotism, because she was Cuban or nothing like that, because she is a good singer and on top of that was recommended by Miguelito Valdes which we grew up together and everybody just got together and say: 'Okay, let's go to and record', that's all; and we went up there and .....
Miguelito says that he bought you fellows a few bottles of liquor and that was the payment.
Uh- Huh. Do you remember if any of those numbers that Olga Guillot recorded with your band, went on to be big hits?
I think 'Sangre son Colora' was a good number and she made a few more that become established....

.. there is no question. The arrangement was made by Rene Hernandez and you know Rene, he was a master in that particular thing and she was established. From that recording she was established; then she come back to Havana, start to record in Havana and that is history about Olga Guillot.
Did Chano ever sit-in with your band on any of these recordings?

..... as a matter of fact, in that particular recording, we sent the conga player to buy a few things and we used that time that he was out - because that was the Nola Studio - there was about seven or eight floors and by that time, you know, the time that he spent, we record one number, 'Sangre son Colora'. I think that Chano was playing the conga.
